title: Inspect and maintain the Nucleus service
summary: Inspect service readiness and owned admission holds, and interpret installation, drain, restart, backup, and recovery guarantees.
use_when: Nucleus health, service selection, admission holds, drain, installation, backup, restore, restart, or removal must be understood or operated.
do_not_use_when: The actual question is requester-domain success, permission to retry lost work, or authority to clear another owner's hold.
outcome: The service state, owned maintenance condition, or installation/recovery evidence is observed through supported interfaces.
effects: Health and service reads expose runtime state. Maintenance creates or releases durable run-owned holds.
Restart terminates the daemon; startup marks unfinished attempts lost. Installation can replace programs and service configuration or migrate state; uninstall retains state and logs.
authority: Nucleus owns its current-user service, socket, state, runtime readiness, and maintenance holds.
Requesters own workflow settlement, domain evidence, and retry decisions; a coordinator releases only its own holds.
success: Installation completes program, provider, and service setup under the applicable owned hold and drain. It performs no artifact-integrity, persistent-state-integrity, or operational-readiness checks. Ordinary service diagnostics establish their separate observations.
Requester admission is reported separately because a quota pause can remain after successful installation.
failure_and_recovery: Quiesce requesters before interruptions when admitted work must finish. Preserve named holds and recovery evidence when ownership or drain is unproved.
Use the retained cutover journal and exact candidate for supported recovery; never roll credentials or an incompatible database backward.
privacy: Service state, credentials, logs, cutover journals, quota files, and backups are private. Database/mailbox records may contain complete prompts, sources, and tool values.
Credential backup/recovery remains separate from database and program rollback; a Nucleus backup does not replace requester backups.
does_not_authorize: Interrupting active attempts without task authority, deleting retained data, retrying requester work, or clearing another hold or failure halt.
Restoring an older credential or incompatible database/binary pair.

consumers.statement: The current user, deployment coordinator, and bounded status readers may inspect and operate the per-user service within their own authority.

preconditions.statement: Service changes select programs, documentation, a Codex runtime path, and private state. Coordinated replacement requires the run's sole drained hold and its activity guard.
Requesters must finish admitted multi-job workflows before Nucleus is held; a free process list alone does not prove durable settlement.

inputs.statement: Maintenance POST requests accept exactly {"run_id":"OWNER"}; commands select that exact owner. Deployment settings accept only string codex_bin and codex_home absolute paths, not credential bytes.
Installation and recovery select program, provider-bundle, harness path, and retained journal metadata without integrity proofs.

outputs.statement: Health reports protocol/harness identity, readiness, admission, maxActiveJobs=8, activeJobs and availableSlots. Maintenance status returns protocol_version=1, holds, drained and nonterminal_jobs.
status-snapshot reads health plus maintenance detail with a 250 ms maintenance bound, without account usage, job content or logs; missing detail is incomplete evidence.

data_semantics.statement: acceptingJobs is admission readiness, not spare capacity. Ordinary health prints diagnostics and exits nonzero unless compatible, authenticated, and accepting.
Drain requires no admission guard, accepted/running/waiting job, or supervised terminal cleanup. Documentation presence and matching files alone do not prove the resident daemon or domain success.

identity_and_units.statement: Run ID owns a durable hold. Maintenance protocol version is 1; execution capacity counts attempts and status-snapshot maintenance wait is at most 250 ms.
The standard service owns its filesystem-protected socket, mode-0600 database, mode-0700 state directory, LaunchAgent, installed programs, private logs and credential home.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Readiness reflects the live runtime at observation time. Installation does not invoke health. A deployment hold still requires its sole matching owner and complete drain.
No service-availability or general response-latency objective is promised.

access.statement: The supported standard surfaces are the current-user CLI and version-one HTTP protocol over Nucleus's filesystem-protected Unix socket.
Local filesystem ownership and permissions protect the socket and private state; version one has no application-level authentication protocol.
No TCP endpoint, cross-user service, catalog-granted access, or direct SQLite integration is supported.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Holds survive process exit with no silent expiry. They refuse new submissions with HTTP 503 deployment_maintenance while exact existing replay and admitted work can continue; release removes only the named owner.

The installer journals service-cutover ownership and exact candidates before replacement. Recovery reinstalls and starts the recorded candidate; successful setup removes the journal without health or exact-copy checks.
Unfinished work or unknown ownership keeps admission held. Credential recovery moves only forward. Schema changes prohibit incompatible binary-only rollback; uninstall retains state/logs.

operational_limits.statement: Deployment runs no model jobs or synthetic requester records. Service installation starts the daemon without waiting for migration, compaction, or health. There is no automatic backup/restore command or general output pruning.
No database-capacity, retention-horizon, or general service support/deprecation bound is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Matched CLI, daemon, installer and provider releases retain independent protocol/store/adapter/harness meanings. Staging records runtime file hashes for ordinary admission checks without validating them. Selected upgrades use the staged runtime unless settings provide codex_bin.

Schema-two cutover preserves jobs/attempts/registrations/cancellation/terminal state, discards old mixed logs and historical answered mailbox rows, and blocks on live pending calls. Pending compaction marker 1000002 becomes 2 only after successful VACUUM and truncating checkpoint; incompatible recovery needs a matching database/binary pair.
Startup retires only terminal records of the removed reserved built-in deployment probe; dependencies or unfinished work block that retirement. It is not a general pruning API.

reliances.statement: Live admission readiness relies on the exact adapter-proved Codex runtime and its account service; no installed Chancery contract covers that external behavior.
The standard always-on macOS service relies on launchd. Foreground protocol use does not establish launchd readiness; no installed Chancery contract covers launchd.
